about: Templates: fill in <app>, <src> (a local checkout), <vibe>, <core benefit>, <media> and <design-system-artifact-url> for an app you can film. Pick an app you have the right to show; assertions are graded by a human or an LLM judge against the outputs and transcript.

evals.name: landing-hero
evals.prompt: make a 20s promo for <app> (repo at <src>) for the top of our landing page. <vibe>, 16:9
evals.expected_output: A ~20s 1920x1080 MP4 showing <app> with a populated demo world, framed screen recordings, captions, logo intro and CTA end card; user's checkout untouched.
assertions: outputs/promo-16x9.mp4 exists and is a playable H.264 video
Video is 16:9 at 1080p or higher (e.g. 1920x1080)
Duration is within 17–23 seconds (target 20s)
The user's <app> checkout is unchanged: same HEAD, same git status, same db.sqlite3, same file set
No servers left listening on the run's assigned port range
Most of the video's runtime shows real footage of the <app> UI in use (not only title slides)
Filmed screens are populated: several distinct items and people with images, no empty states, no test/lorem strings
Opens on <app> branding/promise and ends on a branded end card with a call to action
Each on-screen caption is 6 words or fewer
No dev chrome visible: no debug toolbar, error pages, 'localhost'/127.0.0.1 in a URL bar, or framework overlays
Has promo-style motion graphics: framed screen (browser/device), animated captions, and at least one zoom or camera move on the UI
No identifiable real people appear: none of the repo's git authors/contributors by name or photo; other demo-set or free-to-use headshots are fine
In every shot the caption lands over a still screen (≥0.8s) before the on-screen action starts
At most one zoom/punch-in per shot, and at least one shot stays wide the whole time
Graphics use at least two of the app's own design assets beyond logo and colors (its fonts, an illustration/mascot, real content photos in the graphics)
Every script that deletes a database or media runs scripts/guard.sh on its targets first
Zoomed framing holds steady: no back-and-forth camera slide within a single zoom
The moments follow one thread: the same item/person/project carries across shots
Brand art is current (what the live app shows) (not retired art still in the repo's asset folders)
Captions describe the user's control, not an overclaimed outcome (e.g. 'You approve', not 'You say yes')
End card shows 8–12 photo bubbles filling the space around the text

evals.name: landing-design-system
evals.prompt: make a 20s promo for <app> (repo at <src>) for the top of our landing page, 16:9. use our <design system> for the look: <design-system-artifact-url> . i also put two photos in <media>, use them if they fit
evals.expected_output: A ~20s 1920x1080 MP4 of <app> footage dressed in the supplied design system (its colors, fonts, radius and shadows), logo from the app; supplied third-party film stills flagged as IP and kept off screen.
assertions: outputs/promo-16x9.mp4 exists and is a playable H.264 video
Video is 16:9 at 1080p or higher
Duration is within 17–23 seconds
The user's <app> checkout is unchanged
No servers left listening on the run's assigned port range

The design system was read with Claude's Artifact tool when the session has it (project/README.md and project/tokens.json), never fetched with curl or a web fetch; without the tool, the agent asked the user for an export. Nothing was published to it
promo.json brand colors (background, primary, accent, text) come from the design system's tokens, not the app's CSS
Headline and caption fonts are the design system's families, loaded and visible on the sheet
Frame radius and shadow follow the design system's tokens
Mood matches the design system's theme (a dark-only system gives bold-dark or a dark custom background)
One custom touch drawn from the brand book (e.g. magenta/cyan misregistration on display type, halftone, stepped motion)
If the design system has no logo, the logo comes from the app and reads on the system's background
Supplied third-party film stills never appear on screen; what was taken from them as mood reference is named in the report/README
The storyboard/report surfaces any conflict between the design system and the app's own look on its Look line
README records the design source, which brand fields came from it, and each supplied media file and how it was used
Most runtime is real <app> footage with a populated demo world, short captions, branded intro and CTA end card
